name: High Tory
summary: High Toryism is the older, traditionalist wing of British conservatism. It holds that society is an organic, hierarchical inheritance held together by crown, established Anglican church and landed elite, with the privileged owing paternal duty to those below. It distrusts commercial individualism, neoliberalism, equality and abstract rationalist reform, as well as state socialism.
scope: The profile represents High Toryism as it runs from the seventeenth-century Tories (Filmer's patriarchal royalism, the Church in Danger cry) through Burke's defence of inherited institutions and the Victorian Tories (Derby, Salisbury) to modern traditionalists such as Roger Scruton and the Cornerstone Group. It excludes One-Nation Disraelian reformism, Thatcherite neoliberalism, and the Jacobite and divine-right absolutism of the earliest period where modern adherents have dropped them.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: High Tories accept private enterprise but reject commercial-class values and neoliberalism, and Scruton wants markets embedded in custom and morality rather than left to allocate everything.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke ties liberty and social order to inherited property, and High Tories defend the landed gentry, though the Tory view is of property with duties rather than an absolute right.

regulate-corporations.rationale: High Tories condemn the selfish values of the commercial middle class and favour paternalistic corporatism over individualism, implying support for restraining corporate power.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Cornerstone defends ancient liberties against politically correct censorship, which points against speech codes.

strong-leader.rationale: High Tories favour constitutional monarchy, established institutions and gradualism rather than a leader bypassing the constitution; Burke defends settled inherited arrangements.

state-harmful.rationale: High Toryism treats the state, crown and church as organic authorities that sustain society and hold that obedience is the principal civic virtue (Scruton, SEP).

empower-police-military.rationale: Hierarchy, order and authority are central, and Victorian High Tories backed the empire and navy; Scruton's conservatism prizes authority.

decide-locally.rationale: Organic local community and oikophilia appeal, but Cornerstone opposes devolving power away from the UK centre, so adherents split.

traditional-family.rationale: Cornerstone explicitly champions traditional family and marriage, and High Toryism values a rooted, traditional and patriarchal society.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Cornerstone supports traditional marriage; Scruton moderated his earlier views, so the answer is disagreement but not strong.

more-religion-public.rationale: Church of England establishment and religion are central, and High Tories rallied to the Church in Danger.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Rooted tradition, flag and monarchy and proper pride in the UK are core Cornerstone themes, and Burke defends inherited custom.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke's change proceeding by reference to antiquity and organic gradual flux are the classic statement of the position.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Cornerstone calls for lower immigration (a claim flagged as unsourced on its page) and the Monday Club tradition is restrictionist.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Cornerstone opposes transfers of power upward to the EU, and Tory tradition defends the national constitution.

free-trade.rationale: High Tories favour protectionism and reject neoliberal free trade.

open-borders.rationale: Rooted nation, organic community and Cornerstone's lower-immigration stance make this a clear rejection.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Stewardship of land appeals but distrust of radical state programmes; sources silent and adherents split.

revolution-justified.rationale: Filmer denies any popular right to depose rulers and Burke condemns revolutionary innovation, though he accepted 1688 as restoration of precedent.

central-planning.rationale: High Tories reject state socialism as a threat to rooted life.

land-value-tax.rationale: The tradition was formed in resentment of the land tax and defends landed property.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Burke's partnership of generations rests on inheritance of property and titles, so heavy taxation of inheritances undermines the landed continuity High Tories defend.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protectionism is documented as a High Tory economic position.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wholly alien to a tradition that accepts private enterprise and hierarchy.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Neither stated nor central; the establishment-minded instinct favours existing institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Paternalistic corporatism is documented as a High Tory preference.

one-party-rule.rationale: Contradicts constitutional monarchy and inherited institutions; ideological party rule is the kind of abstract politics Burke attacks.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Monarchism and royalism are listed High Tory principles, Cornerstone cites commitment to the monarchy, and Filmer defended hereditary kingship.

democracy-best.rationale: High Tories prefer traditional hierarchy and the Reform Act cost gentry privilege; they accept parliamentary democracy but not as the supreme principle.

direct-votes.rationale: Burke prefers representation by experienced, propertied men over direct popular rule, and the tradition resisted franchise extension.

workers-councils.rationale: Councils of workers as the basis of power would replace the crown, peerage and Parliament that the High Tory constitution rests on, so adherents reject it.

right-to-secede.rationale: Cornerstone defends the integrity of the UK against devolution; Tory unionism.

natural-rulers.rationale: High Tories regard the traditional gentry as a higher standard and prefer a hierarchical society to equality.

political-violence-never.rationale: Rejection of rebellion pulls toward agreement but support for armed force and Jacobite history makes it contested.

war-builds-character.rationale: Sources are silent; chivalric honour appeals but a Tory bias against warmongering abroad is documented in the eighteenth century.

separate-church-state.rationale: The Church of England establishment is central and Cornerstone supports it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: They want Christian ethics and established church but not scripture as direct law; the common-law tradition remains.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The crown, courts and armed forces are institutions of the state defended as organic authorities.

military-superiority.rationale: Victorian High Tories backed empire and navy, and Cornerstone-style patriotism supports strong defence.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Class harmony under noblesse oblige is a defining claim; class conflict as history's engine is a Marxist thesis.

equal-outcomes.rationale: High Toryism prefers a hierarchical society to modern equality, so it does not accept equal outcomes as a social goal.

self-interest-moral.rationale: High Tories condemn the selfish commercial values of the middle class and teach duty.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Noblesse oblige and Scruton's view of obedience and belonging place duties first; Cornerstone stresses family and community duties.

limit-population.rationale: Sources are silent; traditional family values lean against it.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Agrarian and anti-commercial sentiment is present, but they accepted empire and industrial Britain; split.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Directly opposed to disruptive change of existing institutions; Burke warns against the spirit of innovation.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: The sources never touch on encryption, and authority-minded instincts balance against ancient-liberties arguments, so this is split.

restore-past-order.rationale: They value rooted tradition but Burke and the SEP distinguish conservatism from reaction and say a state needs means of change; adherents split.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Oakeshott's anti-ideological disposition and Burke's rejection of abstraction support judging by experience.

direct-action.rationale: Change by direct action sidesteps the parliamentary and constitutional order that Burke and the High Tory tradition defend.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Rejects primitivism; they defend civilisation, high culture and gentlemanly virtues.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Hierarchical organic society presupposes differentiated functions.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution by need regardless of work or wealth is a communist principle that conflicts with hierarchy and inherited property.

profit-exploitation.rationale: They accept private enterprise and class harmony; exploitation theory is Marxist.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Working-class rule over the former ruling classes is the reverse of the gentry-led order High Tories defend and rests on revolution, which they reject.

collective-farming.rationale: Though agrarian in sentiment, High Tories defend landed estates and individual proprietors rather than collectivised farms.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Marxist thesis rejected; Victorian High Tories supported empire as a national policy.

taxation-theft.rationale: High Tories treat the state and crown as legitimate organic authorities, and they historically resented the land tax without denying the state's right to tax.

harm-principle.rationale: Paternalism holds that the state promotes the welfare, religion and morality of its subjects.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Burke rejects abstract individual rights in favour of inherited liberties, and community duties come first.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit as the main check is a libertarian idea; Tory view rests on rooted belonging.

state-as-business.rationale: Contrary to rooted organic community and the state as an authority.

media-academia-power.rationale: Scruton railed against an intellectual elite's contempt for historic loyalties (oikophobia), so mild agreement.

organic-representation.rationale: Burke and organic community support representation through estates and local bodies, though parties are accepted in practice.

total-state.rationale: The tradition rejects both capitalism run wild and state socialism, and an all-directing state contradicts its reliance on church, family and local community.

national-rebirth.rationale: Gradualism and continuity with the inherited order stand against any call for a radical national rebirth.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Victorian High Tories supported empire but earlier ones opposed expansion; split.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Neo-feudalism is noted by Heywood, but modern adherents do not advocate oath-based rule; split.

bound-labor.rationale: Neo-feudal paternalism noted, but no modern High Tory defends legal bondage.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Hierarchy and paternalistic corporatism oppose democratic control of firms.

economic-freedom.rationale: They reject neoliberal views of freedom, so mildly against this thesis.

rule-by-example.rationale: Gentlemanly virtue and noblesse oblige hold that elite conduct sets the standard.

national-self-determination.rationale: Cornerstone defends the unitary UK against devolution, which cuts against self-government for every nation, while national pride cuts the other way; split.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Religion is central and Burke defends prejudice and inherited wisdom over bare reason.

class-collaboration.rationale: Class harmony through noblesse oblige is a defining feature.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Heritage and high culture are core High Tory concerns, and Burke defends inherited institutions against innovators, so sacrificing museums or libraries for new creation is rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: They prefer a hierarchical and patriarchal society, though modern adherents rarely support legal distinction.

ban-interest.rationale: Banning lending at interest would upset the landed and commercial property system that High Toryism accepts, though it distrusts commercial values.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not a High Tory principle, though the Monday Club's apartheid support is recorded; mainstream adherents reject it.

state-class-instrument.rationale: Marxist doctrine; High Tories see the state as organic authority.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Cultural preservation and rooted identity favour assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial thesis not part of mainstream High Toryism, though restrictionist.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: They favour traditional patriarchal society and would not frame it as injustice.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Not an established position and moral-religious tradition resists.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Paternalism says the state promotes welfare, religion and morality of subjects.

socialism-one-country.rationale: A debate internal to Marxism that High Tories do not engage in, so the answer is neutral.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: A Hindu-nationalist issue with no foothold in British High Toryism, and rural meat-farming traditions oppose it.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religion in public life and established church favour religious instruction.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine about socialist states that is outside High Toryism, so the answer is neutral.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Filmer rejects popular origin of power, though modern Tories accept parliamentary consent; Burke defends inherited rather than consent-based authority.

population-transfer.rationale: Forced removal of minorities is not part of the High Tory tradition, which values ancient liberties and Christian moral order.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The state's coercive authority is accepted as legitimate, so an absolute ban on initiating force is not the High Tory view.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: They reject commercial middle-class competitive values in favour of community.

vanguard-party.rationale: A disciplined revolutionary party is the opposite of High Tory politics, which defends inherited institutions and rejects revolution.

priority-to-poor.rationale: Noblesse oblige supports care but not legal priority; split.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Property-owning democracy is a Thatcherite theme; High Tories are divided.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The sources are silent, and adherents may follow Malthusian conservatism or paternalist social duty, so this is split.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Filling offices by lottery contradicts the belief that some are naturally better suited to rule and the gentry's claim to leadership.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Authority and order pull toward agreement, while defence of ancient liberties pulls against it; the sources do not decide it.

party-controls-media.rationale: Cornerstone defends ancient liberties against censorship, and party-controlled media contradicts that.

party-commands-army.rationale: In the High Tory view the armed forces serve the crown and the constitution, not a party.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The tradition values gentlemanly independent leaders of means and rejects the idea of representatives paid as workers.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Burke famously held representatives to independent judgement.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Cornerstone opposes transferring power upward to the European Union and defends the UK's central government.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Historic crown prerogative appeals; modern constitutional monarchy delegates this; split.

church-by-bishops.rationale: High Church Anglicanism is governed by bishops, so adherents hold episcopal government to be right.

clerical-rule.rationale: High Tories want an established church allied with the crown, not rule by clergy, so this is rejected.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Moral traditionalism supports protecting character, while Cornerstone defends ancient liberties against censorship; split.

recall-officials.rationale: Burke held that representatives owe independent judgement, not mandates removable at will.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Landed estates and tenancy are the traditional gentry economy, so banning renting contradicts it.

people-in-arms.rationale: Modern High Tories back the Crown's regular forces, but Country Tories in the 1690s defended the militia against a standing army, so the rejection is weaker than strong; this is an inference.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Agrarianism and the landed gentry's rural virtues are linked to High Toryism.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Scruton attacked intellectual elites but High Tories prize high culture and learning; split.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They hold that gentry culture is a higher standard and that Western heritage deserves defence.

death-penalty.rationale: Authority favours it but Anglican moral tradition is divided and modern Tories are split.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religion matters but Anglican establishment accommodates evolution; mildly against.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Scruton and Burke treat custom and prejudice as inherited wisdom, so conformity pressure is not a harm in their view.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burke condemns rewriting a constitution from abstract principle.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Hereditary monarchy is the High Tory preferred form of head of state, and Cornerstone cites commitment to the monarchy.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Property carries duties under noblesse oblige rather than absolute rights.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: A dispute among Marxists; High Tories reject Soviet communism regardless of its label, so they are neutral on the label.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: High Tories defend church independence and establishment against curbs on its power; the Church in Danger cry.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Constitutional monarchy as above party is the core symbolic claim, and Cornerstone cites the monarchy.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Filmer's divine right is historic; modern High Tories do not say divine descent, but the monarch's sacral role exists in Anglican coronation. Split.

character-from-environment.rationale: Burke and tradition treat inherited nature and breeding as significant; mild.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Filmer held the king above positive law, but modern High Tories accept the constitution and Burke's inherited liberties.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Crown, peerage and Commons as in Burke's inheritable crown, peerage and privileges.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: A Marxist-Leninist doctrine entirely outside High Toryism, which rejects class struggle and socialism.

land-redistribution.rationale: The landed gentry are the base of the tradition and Burke ties liberty to inherited landed property.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Not a theme in the British High Tory tradition, which defends existing borders and the Union.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Established Anglicanism accepted toleration after 1689, so criminalising leaving a religion is not part of the tradition.

women-must-cover.rationale: Compulsory dress codes for women are alien to the English High Tory tradition.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Cornerstone favours a unitary state and common national culture over separate self-governing minority institutions.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: This Marxist thesis conflicts with the High Tory emphasis on religion, tradition and inherited institutions as shaping society.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Tradition values inherited constitution and institutions over majority will.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: High Toryism prefers a hierarchical and patriarchal order and rejects quota-style egalitarian engineering.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Protectionism is documented but a shut-off bloc is far beyond it, and the tradition accepts overseas commerce under empire; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: Duty is stressed by noblesse oblige but the tradition accepts private enterprise and incentives, so adherents are split.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Revolution is rejected by Filmer and by Burke, so a small armed group provoking one is also rejected.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Defence of inheritable crown and peerage in Burke and High Tory tradition.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Victorian High Tories backed empire; modern adherents may be divided.

patriotic-education.rationale: Cornerstone speaks of proper pride in the UK, the flag and the monarchy, which supports teaching loyalty to the nation.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The sources do not take a view on capitalist crisis, and the tradition is critical of commercial values but not collapse-minded.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Burke prefers inherited liberties to written abstract declarations.

elective-rulers.rationale: Hereditary succession is the Tory position against elective kingship, from Filmer's heirs of the first fathers onward.

minority-veto.rationale: A veto for dissenting individuals contradicts the tradition's emphasis on authority and obedience.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Filmer denies it but Burke accepts 1688 as precedent; split within the tradition.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Early Tories wanted a strong monarchy as counterweight, modern ones accept parliament; split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: The elite's duty to all of society is central to High Toryism.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The landed elite's duty of public service and noblesse oblige reject withdrawal from public affairs.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: A dependency-theory claim from the left, outside the High Tory tradition, which defended empire.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Leadership by descendants of pre-colonial peoples would overturn the established order that High Tories defend.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Burkean continuity with inherited institutions and Scruton's oikophilia support preserving monuments of the past.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Armed forces loyal to the crown but not a political guardian role in the British tradition.

filial-duty.rationale: Filmer ties obedience to rulers to the duty to honour one's father, and the tradition prizes a patriarchal order.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.

reviewHistory.rationale: Burke held representatives to independent judgement, not binding instruction by those who chose them.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Nulled (statement review, 2026-11-11): its value turns on whether representatives must follow binding instructions, and the statement now asks only whether voters can recall them at any time.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

land-use-tenure.rationale: Land held only while used contradicts inherited landed property, central to the gentry tradition.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Treating unequal outcomes as proof of discrimination conflicts with a tradition that accepts hierarchy and rejects egalitarian engineering.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: They reject commercial middle-class values as corrosive of community.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Scruton holds that obedience is the principal civic virtue; Filmer likewise.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities are not part of the High Tory tradition's stated positions.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Cornerstone supports traditional marriage and family, which this abolition contradicts.

informal-organisation.rationale: Small informal groups replace institutions, whereas High Toryism holds that established institutions embody inherited wisdom.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Cornerstone opposes supranational control and defends sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Cornerstone emphasises England's Anglican heritage and the established church in national identity.

religion-illusion.rationale: Religion is central to High Toryism, which champions the established church and religious ethics.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Mixed: they accept enterprise yet critique commercial values.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The Salisbury Review opposed feminism, and the tradition upholds a traditional patriarchal order over economic transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Public provision of housework and childcare would displace the traditional family that Cornerstone holds is the foundation of society.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: The tradition sees both capitalism and state socialism as threats to rooted life.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Denial is rejected by mainstream conservatives, and the sources report no High Tory support for it.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Scruton, the leading modern High Tory thinker, moved away from his earlier defence of revulsion, and criminalisation is not a Cornerstone stance.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Cornerstone defends ancient liberties, and suppression of opposition is not part of the tradition.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: An Islamic religious doctrine with no place in the High Tory tradition.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Filmer rejects deposing rulers, and High Tories value obedience.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Burke wants representation by experienced, propertied men, and the tradition rejects mass direct participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: This critical framework rests on egalitarian premises that High Toryism rejects in favour of hierarchy.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: High Tories define themselves against Whigs, liberals and neoconservatives, and most place themselves on the right, but some (the Red Tory affinity) claim to stand outside the left-right axis; this is an inference.

alienated-labor.rationale: A Marxist concept; High Tories accept private enterprise, though they criticise commercial values, so mild disagreement.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Filmer derived royal authority from God and High Tories tie monarchy to the established Church, but the scope sets aside divine-right absolutism where modern adherents have dropped it, as the audit's own sacred-ruler answer does.

social-market-economy.rationale: Paternalistic corporatism and Scruton's markets embedded in custom resemble a social market economy.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Victorian High Tories supported the empire and navy, and strong defence is part of the tradition.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Hereditary succession is basic to Tory monarchism and Filmer's heirs.

property-franchise.rationale: Tories opposed franchise extension historically; modern adherents split.

domination-women-nature.rationale: An ecofeminist claim that conflicts with the tradition's acceptance of a traditional, patriarchal order.

reification.rationale: A Marxist concept not found in High Tory sources, so mild disagreement.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The tradition defends property and ancient liberties of press and assembly, rejecting this left critique.

racial-franchise.rationale: A racial franchise is not a mainstream High Tory position, though Wikipedia notes apartheid support in the Monday Club.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not an Anglican position in the modern tradition, and not recorded in the sources.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Consumer boycotts of religious minorities are not part of the tradition.

citizens-assembly.rationale: High Tories defend inherited institutions and representation by an established elite and reject popular consent as a source of authority, so lot-drawn bodies that help decide would be an abstract innovation.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: The tradition upholds the established Anglican church as a pillar of society, so a state promoting unbelief is the opposite of its settlement.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: The tradition never addressed extinction risk; its caution about change and concern for inheritance pull in different directions.

abolish-ip.rationale: The tradition defends inherited property, and patents and copyrights are property rights; Burke defended prescriptive property against abstract reform.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: The tradition upholds just war, the defence of the realm and the right of the community to defend itself; absolute non-violence is rejected.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Burke and later Tories stress the nation as an inheritance in continuous succession from the ancestors, an unbroken entailed inheritance.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: The tradition honours the fallen as national heroes and sacrifice for the nation, though 'saints' is stronger than the Anglican tradition allows.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: High Tories hold religion and the established church as the moral basis of order, but treat politics as the preservation of order, not a cosmic struggle; split.

god-not-male.rationale: High Tories defend the established Anglican church and traditional liturgy and language, which describe God in male terms.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The tradition holds that scripture and church tradition judge society, not the other way round.

second-chamber.rationale: Burke defends inherited institutions such as the peerage, and Tories stress the Lords as a check on the elected house.

person-over-state.rationale: Burke's society is an organic partnership of generations in which the individual is subordinate to the whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: High Toryism defends the established Anglican church and holds that society rests on religious foundations.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Tories accept wars of national interest and the empire, but no stand on defensive-only wars is documented.

future-generations.rationale: Burke describes society as a partnership between the living, the dead and those yet to be born, so each generation must hand on its inheritance intact.

women-distinct-values.rationale: High Tories value traditional sex roles and distinct duties but do not argue for giving women's outlook more political weight; adherents are split.

capital-controls.rationale: Protectionist and anti-commercial strands favour national control of wealth, but the tradition also defends property; adherents split and the sources are silent.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Burke explicitly condemns tearing down inherited institutions and defends gradual reform by reference to antiquity.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Burke rejects abstract rationalist experimentation on society in favour of inherited, tested arrangements.

sacred-nation.rationale: Burke describes society as a partnership of the dead, the living and the unborn, and the Cornerstone Group stresses faith, flag and family, but the reverence attaches to inherited society and institutions more than to a sacralised nation.

workers-own-party.rationale: Organic, hierarchical society and class duty run against a class-based workers' party; Tories seek harmony between orders.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Common-law remedies fit the Burkean tradition but paternal state action is also accepted; Scruton favoured local and common-law solutions, so adherents are split.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: High Toryism defends the established Anglican church as the national church with a privileged legal position.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Burke rests legitimacy on inherited institutions rather than popular choice, but that concerns whether democracy is good, not how it is defined; no position on the definition is stated.

defend-planned-state.rationale: High Toryism distrusts state socialism, so defending a state-owned planned economy is not part of it.

national-church-status.rationale: The established Anglican church is a defining pillar of High Toryism, and Burke defends the church establishment as part of the constitution.

simple-living.rationale: Paternalist landed tradition is neither ascetic nor commercially abundant; adherents are split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Burke's inheritance of an ancestral estate and Scruton's oikophilia make attachment to the inherited land and a duty to preserve it central.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Burke defends inherited institutions, parliament and intermediate bodies, and rejects any leader ruling over them.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: High Toryism defends the established Anglican church as part of the constitution, so it accepts a religious dimension to politics.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The paternalist, one-nation strand holds that national loyalty and duty of the privileged to those below go together.

missingStatements.text: Traditional rural pursuits such as hunting with hounds should be protected by law.
missingStatements.rationale: Scruton, the leading modern High Tory thinker, strongly defended fox hunting, and rural gentry life is central to the tradition.
missingStatements.declined: Narrow single-issue (British fox hunting) position; the underlying rural-tradition stance is covered by rural-life-healthier and preserve-national-culture.

notes: Modern Cornerstone-style High Toryism differs from the early Filmerian strand on consent, resistance and divine right; the answers follow the modern mainstream where they differ. Many answers are low-confidence inferences because the tradition is mainly defined by temperament and institutions rather than policy.
